findings.issue: rfb7 (Windows-shaped quoted interpreter paths) exercises the product's existing narrowing and is not tied to either failure mechanism of the CI run; it cannot show the rig fix. It adds coverage, loses none.
findings.resolution: None needed; optionally note in the fragment that rfb7 is a guard against a mis-hypothesis, not a proof of the fix.

findings.issue: rfb8 tests the test rig itself (the fake sweep's recorder), and on POSIX only its one-record-file-per-call clause can fail on the old append design; the overwrite itself is unreproducible off Windows, so the Windows mechanism is removed by construction (O_CREAT|O_EXCL numbered file per call, no shared write offset) rather than by a case that goes red here.
findings.resolution: Acceptable; the design is the fix. No action.

intent.note: Clause (1) asks for one numbered record file per call (O_CREAT|O_EXCL), one reader, rfb1 asserting the exact call list, rfb7/rfb8 added: _CALL_RECORD (test_run_test_gate.py:12114) opens os.path.join(log, '%06d') with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_BINARY, retries on FileExistsError, writes the line and closes; both fake sweeps (_PER_SUITE_SWEEP, _CALL_LOG_SWEEP) use it via _with_call_record; the three readers now go through _ps_calls/_ps_record_files/_ps_lines; rfb1 now asserts sorted(k2) == ['tests/test_t.py tests/test_v.py','tests/test_u.py'] (strictly stronger than the old len(k2)==2 and 'in'); rfb7 and rfb8 exist. Windows mechanism check: no two calls share a file or a write offset, os.makedirs(exist_ok=True) is race-safe, O_EXCL on an existing file is FileExistsError on Windows, readers only run after both processes have exited, and _ps_remove removes dirname(log) so the new calls directory is still cleaned. Clause (2): _slow_answer now loops on time.monotonic until the gap has passed; the drive brackets run_verb with time.monotonic (drive-phase.py:14584-14586), so its stage ms is at least the gap that clock saw pass, and the upper bound (<5000) is unchanged; a coarse tick can only lengthen the loop, never shorten it. No case asserts less than before. I ran rfb-block once: exit 0, 807/807, rfb7 and rfb8 PASS. The executor's outcome describes the diff accurately; redFirst not-attempted is consistent with expectRedFirst false.
intent.redFirstBasis: The executor filed not-attempted: regression task with tests.expectRedFirst false, no red owed. I did not see any added case red; rfb8's per-file clause would fail against the old single-file append design by reading, not by observation.
intent.inheritedTestsBasis: tests.gate is one literal command over two whole suites (tests/test_run_test_gate.py, tests/test_drive_phase.py, about 1953 cases); I read only the changed cases and the helpers they touch, not every case the command selects, so no claim either way about unchanged cases.
